blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Between June 2026 and October 2026, detached houses: listings fell from 21 in June to 13 in October (−38.1%), and it took 3.2% of the city’s 247 sales over the period; condos and townhomes: listings was little changed, 8 in June and 8 in October (+0.0%), and it took 0.9% of the city’s 230 sales over the period.
The monthly write-ups singled out Thornhill for detached houses in June (a buyers’ best bet); condos and townhomes in June (a buyers’ best bet).

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Thornhill

items.t: Boundaries: the City publishes no boundary for the neighbourhood or the MLS sub-area: Not verified as an official boundary. Nearby areas: Albion to the southwest, Websters Corners to the southeast, Whonnock to the east, Ruskin further east, and the City of Mission across the eastern boundary.
Combined Maple Ridge community — Detached median $1,131,000; attached median $525,000, expressly NOT Thornhill figures.
Schools, SD42 (Maple Ridge–Pitt Meadows): SD42 has no middle tier — elementary K–7, secondary 8–12.

Transit: TransLink route 748 (Thornhill / Haney Place) is a loop from Haney Place via 240 Street, McClure Drive, Jackson Road, 100 Avenue, 256 Street, 98 Avenue, 264 Street and 268 Street, with weekday and Saturday trips only at wide intervals — that claim rests on route 748's own timetable document. Route 701 runs east on Dewdney Trunk Road along the area's south side, verified on route 701's own timetable. There is no West Coast Express station in this sub-area. Main roads: Dewdney Trunk Road and Lougheed Highway along the south side; 248 Street, 256 Street and 264 Street north–south; 100 Avenue and 112 Avenue east–west on the hillside.
How people search for it: "Thornhill" (board and City name), "Thornhill MR" (MLS form), "Thornhill, Maple Ridge," and "Grant Hill" for the hillside.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Thornhill

items.t: Zoning — City of Maple Ridge Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019: the schedule lists minimum lot areas of A-1 2.0 ha, A-2 4.0 ha, A-3 8.0 ha, RS-2 0.4 ha and RS-3 0.8 ha or 2.0 ha depending on the zone text — the rural zones that cover most of this hillside. Any parcel's actual zone: per-parcel, not verified.

LOUGHEED TRANSIT CORRIDOR — ADOPTED Jan 27, 2026 per the City record: Bylaw 7781-2021 (third reading + adoption Jan 27, 2026; City news release Feb 4, 2026); the corridor ends at 221 Street and does not reach Thornhill.

North 256 Street Industrial Lands Area Plan: the plan covers both sides of 256 Street north of 128 Avenue (about 500 acres, per the City release) at this area's north side; it establishes future designations and does not itself approve construction — disclose it on affected listings as a designation change, not a development approval.

Suites and added units — Maple Ridge / ALR: one secondary suite per lot is permitted in listed zones including A-1, A-2 and A-3, contained within the single detached building, to a maximum of 40% of gross floor area, and not in the Floodplain Area. On ALR parcels, the provincial ALR Use Regulation also governs: one secondary suite in the principal residence (s.31), and an additional residence only if the s.32 conditions are met.

Subdivision and servicing — Maple Ridge: subdivision potential follows the parcel's zone minimums (above) and, where ALR applies, ALC approval (ALR block below) — the zoning minimums only matter if the parcel can actually be subdivided. Wells are recorded in the provincial GWELLS database, and onsite sewerage must comply with the Sewerage System Regulation, including the 30 m setback from a well unless professional advice is obtained.
Property taxes — City of Maple Ridge: 2026 property taxes were due July 2, 2026; a 5% penalty applies to any outstanding balance on July 3, 2026 and an additional 5% on September 2, 2026.

ALR block (applies where a Thornhill parcel is ALR — status per-parcel, not verified here): subdivision within the ALR requires Agricultural Land Commission approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)). Caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Check a parcel on the ALC maps.

The trail network is the amenity (read Nov 1, 2026). The City describes Thornhill's 256 Street trail network for mountain biking and hiking — 17 trails, moderately difficult, typically about an hour to complete, usable year-round — and Kanaka Creek Regional Park (Metro Vancouver) sits at the west side, with the Canyon Trail to Cliff Falls and the Bell-Irving Hatchery. No City recreation centre or library branch sits inside this sub-area; both are in the Town Centre to the west.

Guide-only claims (the Thornhill Park and Hall details, the Thornhill Trails trailhead details, and the SD42 June 2021 facilities-review statements) are not verified site copy, not defects and not facts.
